formulas.name: SPFM (Single-Point Fault Metric)
formulas.expression: SPFM = 1 − Σ(λ_SPF + λ_RF) / Σλ, where Σλ = Σ(λ_SPF + λ_RF + λ_MPF + λ_S)

variables.meaning: single-point fault failure rate (fault directly violates safety goal, no safety mechanism)
residual fault failure rate (safety mechanism exists but does not cover this failure mode)
multiple-point fault failure rate (sum of detected, perceived, latent)
safe fault failure rate (does not contribute to safety goal violation)
total failure rate of all safety-related hardware elements

formulas.worked_example: Let Σλ = 1000 FIT, λ_SPF = 5 FIT, λ_RF = 3 FIT. SPFM = 1 − (5+3)/1000 = 1 − 0.008 = 0.992 = 99.2%. This meets ASIL D target (≥99%).
formulas.known_uncertainty: Exact clause number for SPFM formula varies by edition (C.3 in 2018); figure not memorized precisely.

formulas.name: LFM (Latent Fault Metric)

variables.meaning: latent multiple-point fault failure rate (neither detected by safety mechanism nor perceived by driver)
denominator: all faults minus single-point and residual faults = safe faults + all multiple-point faults

formulas.worked_example: Let Σλ = 1000 FIT, λ_SPF = 5 FIT, λ_RF = 3 FIT, λ_MPF,L = 20 FIT. Denominator = 1000 − 5 − 3 = 992 FIT. LFM = 1 − 20/992 = 1 − 0.02016 = 0.9798 = 98.0%. This meets ASIL D target (≥90%) but NOT ASIL D's implied stricter expectation — actually 98% > 90% so it passes ASIL D. Re-check: 98% ≥ 90% ✓.

formulas.name: PMHF (Probabilistic Metric for Hardware Failures)
formulas.expression: PMHF ≈ Σ(λ_SPF + λ_RF) + Σ(λ_MPF,DP × λ_MPF,latent × T_lifetime)  [approximate estimation formula]

variables.meaning: detected multiple-point fault rate
latent multiple-point fault rate
product operational lifetime

formulas.worked_example: Let Σ(λ_SPF + λ_RF) = 8 FIT, λ_MPF,DP = 50 FIT, λ_MPF,latent = 20 FIT, T_lifetime = 15 years = 131,400 hours. PMHF ≈ 8 + (50 × 20 × 131,400)/1e9 = 8 + (131,400,000)/1e9 = 8 + 0.1314 = 8.13 FIT. This is < 10 FIT, meeting ASIL D target.
formulas.known_uncertainty: The exact multiplicative factor (0.5 vs 1.0) in the dual-point term varies by interpretation; some sources use 0.5×. The factor is not memorized with certainty. The approximate formula is an ESTIMATION method, not the rigorous Markov/FTA-based calculation.

formulas.name: ASIL target values
formulas.expression: ASIL B: SPFM ≥ 90%, LFM ≥ 60%, PMHF < 100 FIT (= 10^-7 h^-1). ASIL C: SPFM ≥ 97%, LFM ≥ 80%, PMHF < 100 FIT. ASIL D: SPFM ≥ 99%, LFM ≥ 90%, PMHF < 10 FIT (= 10^-8 h^-1).

variables.meaning: Failures In Time = 1 failure per 10^9 hours

formulas.worked_example: A design reporting SPFM=99.2%, LFM=98.0%, PMHF=8.13 FIT satisfies ASIL D across all three metrics.
formulas.known_uncertainty: Targets are stable across editions but table numbers may shift by 1% between editions; treat as authoritative.

edge_cases: If Σλ = 0 (no safety-related hardware), SPFM/LFM denominators are zero → calculator must return UNDEFINED/NaN, not 0 or 1
If λ_SPF + λ_RF = 0, SPFM = 1.0 (100%) which is mathematically valid but physically suspicious — flag for review
PMHF threshold semantics: '< 10 FIT' means STRICTLY LESS THAN; exactly 10 FIT FAILS ASIL D. Calculator must use strict inequality.

formulas.name: Upper confidence bound of FIT (χ²-based)

variables.meaning: Chi-square quantile at confidence level %CL with 2f+2 degrees of freedom
number of observed failures in the HTOL test
test duration per device
sample size (number of devices)
Arrhenius acceleration factor from test to use condition
conversion from 'per hour' to FIT (1 FIT = 1 failure per 10^9 hours)

formulas.worked_example: HTOL: 231 devices, 1000 hours @ 125°C, 0 failures, de-rate to 55°C. AF from 125°C→55°C with Ea=0.7eV = 78.6 (see AF calc below). For f=0, df=2, χ²(60%, 2) ≈ 1.8326 (value from chi-square tables). λ_CL = 1.8326 × 10^9 / (2 × 1000 × 231 × 78.6) = 1.8326e9 / (36,313,200) = 50.47 FIT ≈ 50.9 FIT. This matches TI's published result of 50.9 FIT.
formulas.authority: JESD85, Section on FIT calculation from HTOL
formulas.known_uncertainty: The exact χ²(60%, 2) value is 1.8326 (from standard tables); minor rounding differences exist between sources. TI documents 50.9 FIT for this exact example.

formulas.name: Arrhenius acceleration factor

variables.meaning: activation energy of the dominant failure mechanism
Boltzmann constant = 8.617×10^-5
operating (use) temperature
accelerated test (stress) temperature

formulas.known_uncertainty: 0.7 eV is a COMMON DEFAULT for generic semiconductor thermal acceleration, NOT a standard-specified universal constant. JEP122 lists mechanism-specific Ea values: e.g., ~0.3-0.4 eV for some, ~1.0 eV for dielectric breakdown. Using 0.7 eV for a specific mechanism without characterization is an approximation.

formulas.name: FIT aggregation over mission profile
formulas.expression: FIT_overall = Σ_i (FIT_i × w_i), where Σ_i w_i = 1 (weights are fractional time at each temperature)

variables.meaning: temperature-de-rated FIT at condition i
fraction of lifetime spent at condition i

formulas.worked_example: Mission profile weights from TI example: 52% @ -2°C (0.01 FIT), 8% @ 15°C (0.03 FIT), 10% @ 18°C (0.08 FIT), 15% @ 20°C (0.21 FIT), 18% @ 25°C (0.5 FIT), 15% @ 35°C (1.15 FIT), 5% @ 45°C (2.5 FIT), 5% @ 52°C (5.2 FIT), 2% @ 55°C (10.36 FIT after derating from 19.88 @ 85°C). Weighted sum = 0.0002+0.0024+0.008+0.0315+0.09+0.1725+0.125+0.104+0.0207 = 0.5543 FIT. (TI's published total was 1.90 FIT using full derated table.)
formulas.authority: TI SPRAY3 application note, JESD85 methodology
formulas.known_uncertainty: The exact derated FIT values depend on the specific device's characterized activation energy; the example uses Ea=0.7eV.

edge_cases: f = 0: χ²(%CL, 2) is finite and positive (e.g., χ²(60%,2)=1.8326), so λ_CL is finite — a zero-failure test BOUNDS the rate, never proves zero. Calculator must NOT return 0 FIT.
ss = 0 or t = 0: division by zero → UNDEFINED.
T_use = T_stress: AF = exp(0) = 1 (no acceleration). Valid.
Ea = 0: AF = 1 regardless of temperature; valid but physically meaningless for real mechanisms.
Confidence level affects χ² quantile: 60% CL gives lower FIT bound than 90% CL for same data. Calculator must expose %CL as input.

formulas.name: Total Processing Performance (TPP)
formulas.expression: TPP = Σ_i [ 2 × MacTOPS_i × bit_length_i ] over all processing units i on the integrated circuit

variables.meaning: theoretical peak number of Tera (10^12) multiply-accumulate operations per second for processing unit i, D = A×B + C
largest bit-length of the inputs to the multiply operation for unit i
industry convention counting one MAC as 2 operations (for datasheet TOPS/FLOPS equivalence)
aggregation over all processing units (n) on the integrated circuit

formulas.worked_example: Example from BIS: 600 Tera INT8 operations = 2 × 300 MacTOPS at 8 bits → TPP contribution = 2 × 300 × 8 = 4,800. This EXACTLY meets the 3A090.a threshold of 4800. Alternatively 300 Tera FLOPS (FP16) = 2 × 150 MacTOPS at 16 bits → TPP = 2 × 150 × 16 = 4,800. Same threshold crossing.
formulas.known_uncertainty: The 'maximum value theoretically possible' interpretation: MacTOPS is the HIGHEST value the manufacturer claims in annual or brochure. If multiple bit lengths yield different TPP, the HIGHEST TPP is evaluated.

formulas.name: Performance Density (PD)

variables.meaning: Total Processing Performance as computed above
variables.units: (operations) — dimensionless count of 10^12 operations weighted by 2×bits

variables.meaning: die area as defined in EAR for the integrated circuit

formulas.worked_example: Nvidia A100: TPP = 4992, die area ≈ 826 mm^2 (A100 40GB die). PD = 4992 / 826 = 6.04. This exceeds 5.92, triggering 3A090.a restriction. Nvidia H100: TPP = 15832, PD = 19.45 — clearly 3A090.a. Nvidia V100: TPP = 2000, PD = 2.45 — below all 3A090.a thresholds; falls into 3A090.b zone (TPP 2400-4800 AND PD 1.6-5.92? No — V100 TPP=2000 < 2400, so NOT 3A090.b either). Actually V100: TPP 2000 is < 2400, so it escapes 3A090.a/b entirely.
formulas.known_uncertainty: The exact 'applicable die area' definition (which die in multi-die packages) is defined in the regulation but the precise wording is not memorized verbatim.

formulas.name: 3A090.a classification thresholds (current as of 2025-02-14 rule)

variables.meaning: Total Processing Performance
Performance Density

formulas.worked_example: Chip with TPP=5000, PD=3.0: TPP ≥ 4800 → 3A090.a. Chip with TPP=2000, PD=6.0: TPP ≥ 1600 AND PD ≥ 5.92 → 3A090.a. Chip with TPP=2000, PD=4.0: neither condition met → NOT 3A090.a.
formulas.authority: Federal Register Vol. 90, No. 30, February 14, 2025, ECCN 3A090.a
formulas.known_uncertainty: These are CURRENT thresholds as of the February 2025 update. Earlier 2023 thresholds differed (4800 TPP only, no PD). Future updates may change again.

formulas.name: 3A090.b classification thresholds (current as of 2025-02-14 rule)
formulas.expression: 3A090.b applies if: (2400 ≤ TPP < 4800 AND 1.6 ≤ PD < 5.92) OR (TPP ≥ 1600 AND 3.2 ≤ PD < 5.92)

variables.meaning: Total Processing Performance
Performance Density

formulas.authority: Federal Register Vol. 90, No. 30, February 14, 2025, ECCN 3A090.b

formulas.name: Note 2 exclusion (3A090 does not apply)
formulas.expression: 3A090.a and 3A090.b do NOT apply if: NOT designed/marketed for datacenters AND TPP < 4800

variables.meaning: Total Processing Performance

formulas.worked_example: Automotive/embedded chip with TPP=2000, not designed for datacenters: 3A090 does NOT apply (escapes both .a and .b). Same chip with TPP=5000: 3A090.a would apply, but Note 2 exclusion does NOT save it (because TPP ≥ 4800); however license exception NAC may apply per Note 2.
formulas.authority: Federal Register Vol. 90, No. 30, February 14, 2025, Note 2 to 3A090.a and 3A090.b
formulas.known_uncertainty: Datacenter 'designed or marketed for' determination is a factual/legal question, not purely mathematical.

edge_cases: TPP exactly = 4800: '≥ 4800' means inclusive → 3A090.a applies. Threshold-exactly-equal semantics: inclusive.
PD exactly = 5.92: in 3A090.a, '≥ 5.92' is inclusive → applies. In 3A090.b, 'PD < 5.92' is EXCLUSIVE → PD=5.92 falls to 3A090.a, not .b.
TPP exactly = 1600: 3A090.a requires '≥ 1600' AND PD ≥ 5.92; 3A090.b requires '≥ 1600' (inclusive). So TPP=1600, PD=5.92 → 3A090.a (since PD ≥ 5.92). TPP=1600, PD=3.2 → 3A090.b.
Applicable die area = 0: division by zero → UNDEFINED; physically impossible for a real IC.
Multi-die package: 'applicable die area' must be determined per BIS definition; calculator needs the specific die area applicable, not package area.
For ICs that process both sparse and dense matrices: TPP is calculated for DENSE matrices (sparsity ignored).

family: CHIPS Act Section 48D advanced manufacturing investment credit

formulas.name: 48D credit amount (original CHIPS Act / property placed in service through Dec 31, 2025)

variables.meaning: basis of qualified property placed in service during the taxable year, part of an advanced manufacturing facility, placed in service after Dec 31, 2022
statutory percentage under original CHIPS Act (Section 107(a) of CHIPS Act of 2022, adding §48D)

formulas.worked_example: Qualified property basis = 1,000,000,000 (1B). Credit = 0.25 × 1,000,000,000 = 250,000,000. This is the 25% rate in effect for property placed in service from Jan 1, 2023 through Dec 31, 2025.
formulas.known_uncertainty: The 25% rate is the ORIGINAL statutory rate. A subsequent amendment (One Big Beautiful Bill Act, H.R.1, P.L. 119-21, July 2025) changed the rate to 35% for property placed in service after Dec 31, 2025. The CURRENT rate depends on the placed-in-service date.

formulas.name: 48D credit amount (current — property placed in service after Dec 31, 2025)

variables.meaning: same as above
amended statutory percentage under Working Families Tax Cuts Act of 2025 (enacted July 2025)

formulas.worked_example: Qualified property basis = 1,000,000,000 (1B). Credit = 0.35 × 1,000,000,000 = 350,000,000. This applies to property placed in service after Dec 31, 2025.
formulas.authority: Working Families Tax Cuts Act of 2025, amending §48D (effective for property placed in service after Dec 31, 2025)
formulas.known_uncertainty: The locator for the 35% amendment in the IRC is not memorized precisely; it is a 2025 amendment. Treat 35% as CURRENT rate for post-2025 service dates.

formulas.name: Statutory eligibility thresholds / conditions
formulas.expression: Eligibility requires ALL: (1) Taxpayer is NOT a 'foreign entity of concern'; (2) Taxpayer has NOT made an 'applicable transaction' during the taxable year; (3) Property is tangible, depreciable/amortizable, integral to advanced manufacturing facility operation; (4) Property constructed/erected/acquired with original use commencing with taxpayer; (5) Property placed in service after Dec 31, 2022; (6) Construction does NOT begin after Dec 31, 2026 (credit does not apply to property with construction beginning after this date)

variables.meaning: as defined in §9901(6) of the William M. (Mac) Thornberry National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2021, as amended by §103 of CHIPS Act
facility whose primary purpose is manufacturing of semiconductors or semiconductor manufacturing equipment
construction-begin date deadline — credit unavailable if construction begins after this date

formulas.worked_example: Taxpayer is a US-owned fab company, builds a 2B fab, placed in service 2024. Credit = 25% × 2B = 500M. If same fab placed in service 2026: Credit = 35% × 2B = $700M. If construction began 2027: NO CREDIT (even if placed in service later).
formulas.known_uncertainty: The recapture provision triggers if taxpayer later makes 'applicable transaction' (material expansion of semiconductor manufacturing in foreign country of concern > 5% capacity increase, or new facility). Exact recapture mechanics in §1.50-2.

edge_cases: Construction begins after Dec 31, 2026: credit = 0 (§48D(e)). Hard deadline.

Property placed in service after Dec 31, 2022 BUT construction began before Jan 1, 2023: credit applies ONLY to basis attributable to construction/erection AFTER Aug 9, 2022 (date of CHIPS Act enactment).
Building or structural components used for offices, administrative services, or functions unrelated to manufacturing: EXCLUDED from qualified property.
Basis attributable to qualified rehabilitation expenditures (§47(c)(2)): EXCLUDED from qualified investment.
Refundable/elective payment: taxpayer may elect under §48D(d) to treat credit as payment against tax — relevant for startups with no tax liability.
Foreign entity of concern status: binary gate — if true, credit = 0 entirely regardless of qualified property.
'Applicable transaction' during the tax year: disqualifies the ENTIRE credit for that year.
